requirements.requirement: Expose node1's staged projects directory as an authenticated SMB share named projects for the design team.
requirements.summary: The projects share maps only to /srv/legacy2/samba-team-share/projects, permits the design group, is writable, has persistent SELinux labeling, listens on TCP/445, and remained active after restart.

requirements.requirement: From node2, designer must be able to list, read, and update documents using the demonstration credentials in access.txt.
requirements.summary: Node2 derived the designer credentials from access.txt, listed the projects share, downloaded an original drawing, created and overwrote a document, verified its contents, and removed the test artifact. The full workflow also succeeded after both node restarts.

requirements.requirement: Reject guest access and access to sibling directories.
requirements.summary: Guest access returned ACCESS_DENIED; authenticated attempts against the private sibling and parent share returned BAD_NETWORK_NAME; traversal from projects into private returned OBJECT_NAME_NOT_FOUND. These denials were reverified in the final post-restart workflow.

requirements.requirement: Keep the initial drawings in /srv/legacy2/samba-team-share intact.
requirements.summary: Final SHA-256 values for drawing.txt and materials.csv exactly match the preparation baseline, and the final inventory contains no test documents. Protected access.txt and private/contracts.txt also retained their original checksums and restrictive permissions.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: Both nodes remained on RHEL 10.0 with kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0 after execution and restart. Samba 4.23.5 packages came from the configured RHEL 10 repositories, and package-health checks remained successful.

overall_summary: All material outcomes are satisfied with direct final-state and behavioral evidence. The projects share works from node2 with the supplied designer credentials, unauthorized access is rejected, seeded content is preserved, the platform remains unchanged, and functionality persists across verified restarts of both managed nodes.
limitations: Requirement R4 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Package installation, account/group and project-permission changes, Samba configuration with a rollback copy, persistent SELinux labeling, TCP/445 firewall exposure, service enablement, bounded client test writes with cleanup, and node restarts all had clear task or mandatory evidence-protocol roles. Temporary local workspaces and remote test files were removed; no failed services, damaged package state, or unrelated listeners remained. The restart protocol is complete for both nodes: each has a healthy pre-restart state, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state and workflow, with lifecycle boot observations independently corroborating both transitions.
